courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester.

courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health
courses.description: Public health topics will vary with the instructor and semester.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: SPHG
courses.title: Introduction to Public Health
courses.description: This introductory course will describe the history of public health, the key terms and concepts, and how the core areas of public health are integrated to promote health at a population level. The class will engage the students in active learning through the use of media, innovative technology, discussion groups, and field experiences.

courses.subject: SPHG
courses.title: Foundations of Public Health
courses.description: This course is designed to introduce you to public health and help you develop the knowledge and skills necessary to identify and describe public health problems. Restricted to matriculated BSPH majors in BIOS, CGPH, HPM, EHS, and NUTR.

courses.subject: SPHG
courses.title: Public Health Systems and Solutions
courses.description: The course is designed to help you understand and analyze complex health systems and develop the knowledge and skills necessary to develop, implement, and evaluate solutions to public health problems. Restricted to matriculated BSPH majors in BIOS, CGPH, HPM, EHS, and NUTR.

courses.subject: SPHG
courses.title: Public Health Entrepreneurship
courses.description: Basic concept underlying commercial and social entrepreneurship applied to public health, including guest lectures by individuals with proven success in these areas. Honors version available.

courses.subject: SPHG
courses.title: Global Social Entrepreneurship in Public Health
courses.description: This study abroad course will introduce students to basic concepts and case studies of commercial and social entrepreneurship as applied to the pursuit of public health through both for-profit and non-profit entities. This course features guest speakers with successful experience in public health entrepreneurship in diverse arenas as well as those who have experienced challenges or venture failures. Honors version available.

source.text: SPHG 429. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-VALUES, HI-ABROAD.

courses.subject: SPHG
courses.title: Foundations of Public Health
courses.description: By applying crosscutting themes of health equity, history, community engagement and the Gillings's mantra of "Global is Local. Local is Global," students develop foundational knowledge of how public health has evolved, its frameworks, the determinants of health and health disparities through research and practice applications. With this knowledge, students work individually and in teams to apply their learning to a public health problem and propose innovative solutions.

courses.title: Special Topics in Public Health

courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 1 total completions.

courses.subject: SPHG
courses.title: Leading from the Inside-Out
courses.description: This course prepares students for public health practice by introducing fundamental leadership skills necessary to advance health equity and recognize and address challenges in organizational settings. Restricted to MPH students only.
courses.requisites_raw: Pre- or corequisites, SPHG 711, SPHG 712, SPHG 713, SPHG 721, and SPHG 722.

courses.subject: SPHG
courses.title: Practicum Assignments & Interprofessional Practice Activities
courses.description: This course awards credit to required practicum assignments and includes a series of interprofessional practice activities designed to provide healthcare professionals with the foundational skills needed to work in teams to effectively collaborate and coordinate care in population health. Restricted to MPH students only.

courses.subject: SPHG
courses.title: MPH Pre-Practicum Assignments
courses.description: This course provides structures and supports for students as they search, select, and plan for the practicum. It awards credit to required pre-practicum assignments.

courses.title: MPH Pre and Post Practicum Assignments
courses.description: This course provides structures and supports for the practicum search, selection, planning, implementation, and evaluation process. It awards credit to practicum hours and assignments.

courses.title: MPH Post-Practicum Assignments
courses.description: This course facilitates reflection on the practicum and awards credit to required post-practicum assignments.

courses.subject: SPHG
courses.title: Data Analysis for Public Health
courses.description: This introductory course is part of the MPH core curriculum and focuses on the biostatistics and analysis methods commonly found in public health. Students will learn to produce, interpret, and use straight-forward data analyses.

courses.subject: SPHG
courses.title: Methods and Measures for Public Health Practice
courses.description: This course is part of the MPH core curriculum, and introduces epidemiologic concepts and how to describe population patterns of health, health inequities, and their determinants.

courses.subject: SPHG
courses.title: Systems Approaches to Understanding Public Health Issues
courses.description: This course is part of the MPH core curriculum and introduces students to systems thinking approaches to understanding the complex and interconnecting factors that underpin current public health issues.

courses.subject: SPHG
courses.title: Public Health Solutions: Systems, Policy and Advocacy
courses.description: This course introduces students to the health systems and the US health system in particular. It provides an introduction to the role of health policy in addressing public health problems and advancing health equity, and how evidence, law and ethics play a role in policy-making. It provides students with the skills to communicate information about public health problems and solutions to various audiences and introduces them to concepts of public health advocacy.

courses.subject: SPHG
courses.title: Developing, Implementing, and Evaluating Public Health Solutions
courses.description: Students will identify, analyze and prioritize potential public health solutions. In addition, students will learn to adapt evidence-based solutions, engage with community partners, and disseminate solutions. Builds on first semester MPH core courses.
